brief: Natixis expects September nonfarm payrolls to slow from August's pace to +60k (prior 162k), below the 90k consensus, which would bring the three-month moving average to 81k. Leisure/hospitality and local-government gains are expected to normalize down while manufacturing and construction, helped by the data-center buildout, stay solid. Unemployment is expected to rise to a rounded 4.2% as prime-age participation increases further, echoing a similar 5bp participation-driven rise in August despite that month's blowout payrolls. Average hourly earnings are expected at a listless 0.3% m/m. Consumer pessimism about job prospects and tepid wages point to underlying labor-market softness, even though slowing labor supply has kept the unemployment rate stable over the past year. Natixis's core argument: a strong payrolls print alone would not necessarily be hawkish for the Fed, since it would need higher participation, a stable unemployment rate, and higher wages together, so Friday's data should not add pressure for an October hike. A much weaker print, however, would lower the bar for what counts as an acceptable CPI print on October 14. Absent high, broad-based CPI, Natixis sees the path of least resistance as a pause in October and reassessment in December, reinforced by midterm elections falling within a week of the meeting.
